profiles: The pinned native projection releases and name, operator and lexical profiles. MySQL 5.6 and 5.7 provide left-associated UNION. Later pinned releases and PostgreSQL provide UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT.
scope: A binary tree of checked SELECT arms and set operators without row-selection clauses on the compound or its arms. Branches retain their scopes and exactly preserve the first output names.
open: Additional leaf query forms, compound ordering and bounds, WITH, mixed types outside the recorded domain, and larger generated trees

Compound.role: A closed typed set operation on two independently scoped queries
invariants: Both operands have the same profile and nonempty width
Every paired position resolves to a supported native output type
Every arm uses checked result expressions and no local ordering or bound
Depth at most 16 and at most 64 expanded arms
MySQL 5.6 and 5.7 accept UNION with a SELECT right operand
Compound.meaning: UNION ALL adds row multiplicities. INTERSECT ALL takes their minimum. EXCEPT ALL subtracts right multiplicity down to zero. Unmodified operators use support sets. NULLs in a given common output position compare as equivalent for these operations. The first operand supplies ordered column names. PostgreSQL resolves a pair of unknown NULL operands to text and uses the known role where one operand is unknown. MySQL uses the selected integral width. An all-NULL result has a fixed null-only role whose native metadata is recorded by profile and materialization rule.
Compound.sql: Emit operators and explicit ALL where used. Modern MySQL and PostgreSQL enclose nested branches to preserve the tree. MySQL 5.x emits its left spine in infix order.

ResultKind.role: A native output type or a leaf whose bare NULL participates in type determination

analysis: Read operand names and types in their own fact scopes, preserve parenthesized set grouping and normalize explicit DISTINCT to default set semantics. Reject unsupported query modifiers and incompatible type or width before returning a complete value.
observations: Column names and native type tags in first-arm order
Bag of exact typed values and NULLs, including duplicates
Observable grouping when operator and quantifier choices differ

pairs: two ordinary table arms with different rows
finite.completeness: Verify the exact product of registered operators, width, quantifier and operand forms from the inspected values.

negative: Over-depth tree or too many expanded arms
faults: Change set operator or remove a required grouping
trust: Fixed native operator, type and result metadata rules
Server documentation and typed native observations for the supported domains
